lines.text: [hushed, intimate, drawing the listener in] She sent him forty-seven paper planes... before she ever heard his voice.
[warm, a little smile] This is plane number one.
[gentle storyteller] Mira was twenty-two, on the fifth floor of a city that never noticed her.
Across the alley, a stranger kept his lamp on until two a.m. Every single night.
[playful, conspiratorial] One night, she folded her grocery list into a plane... and threw it.
It landed right on his windowsill.
[deadpan] His lamp went off. [small laugh] Great. She'd scared him.
[light, curious] But the next morning... it flew back.
On the back of her list, he'd drawn her. [beat] Badly.
And underneath... a tiny lamp, and a question mark.
[smiling] So that night, she folded plane number two. Just one word. Hi.
[a small gasp, suspense] But the wind had other plans. It dropped five floors, into the alley...
[low, slowing, intrigued] where someone picked it up. [pause] And it wasn't him.
